lines.t: Hoo! Welcome to the Foot Bridge, {name}. Last time you opened Amy's juice stand.
People here measure in inches and feet. But the Smudge got here first. It snapped the rope rail on the bridge!
Rosa makes all the rope in town. Her shed is just up the path. Go say hello.
Hoo! The Math Crew found which of Gus's posts is taller. They each did it their own way.
Walk up to each of them and listen. Then come back and tell me.
Hoo! Two ways, and one answer: the south post is taller by 2 inches.
Which way is most like yours? Write about it on your page, right under the Crew's card.
Walk up to each Crew member and listen to their way first.
Eastside is open, {name}! Next time we visit the General Store over there.
Hoo! Every bridge job on the page gets us one step closer to Eastside.
Hoo! A brick chip? I wonder what the Smudge is building. Keep it, {name}. It's a clue.
The gate is open. Eastside is ours to explore! Next lesson we visit the General Store, where they weigh things in pounds and ounces.

lines.t: The rail is tight, {name}. But look! The Smudge is sitting right on my bridge.
So you're the explorer Rosa told me about! I'm Gus. I keep the Foot Bridge.
Rosa tied your two ropes into one: 2 ft 8 in + 1 ft 7 in = 3 ft 15 in of rope for the broken gap in my rail.
But look at my north post. The Smudge stuck a tag on it. Go read it.
Read that tag on the north post. Something about it looks wrong to me.
Now tie the other end to the south post.
Tight as a drum! Thank you, {name}.
Go on, {name}! Chase that cloud right across my bridge.
Eastside is open, and my rail is the best on the river. Come back any time!
I'm Gus, the bridgekeeper. Nobody crosses until my rope rail is fixed. Safety first!
That's right! 15 inches is 1 foot and 3 inches. Now tie the rope to the south post.
The rail is back! Now people can hold on all the way across.
Eastside wants rope for its side of the bridge, too. Read the Foot Bridge Board on your page, then help Rosa fill their order.

Grr! 27 feet. Fine! Catch me if you can!
Your rail is 9 yards long. That's 12 feet! Heh heh!
6 feet 8 inches?! Ugh. You'll never get past the gate!
Your rope is 80 inches. That's 8 feet!
THIRTY inches?! You measured everything right!
Fine. Keep your silly bridge. My Brick Golem will be ready at the end of Level 10. Heh heh heh…
The Eastside gate is 2 feet 6 inches wide. That's 26 inches! Wrong measure, no entry!

lines.t: My way is feet and inches.
I change the south post's 79 inches to feet and inches. I split 79 into 72 and 7 with a number bond.
72 inches is 6 feet, so the south post is 6 ft 7 in.
Both posts are 6 feet, and 7 inches is 2 more than 5 inches. The south post is taller by 2 inches!
Split 15 inches with a number bond: 12 inches and 3 inches. The 12 inches make the new foot. What is left?
Each yard is 3 feet. Count by 3s nine times, or multiply 9 × 3.
Count by 12s until the next one is too big. When you pass 80, stop and go back one.
Hi, I'm Atlas! Eastside is right across that river, and I've never been there. I can't wait to explore it!
I take out whole feet with a number bond. 46 inches is 36 inches and 10 inches, so it's 3 feet 10 inches.

lines.t: My way is all inches.
I change the north post to inches. 6 feet is 6 × 12, so 72 inches.
72 inches and 5 more inches make 77 inches. The south post is 79 inches.
79 − 77 = 2. The south post is taller by 2 inches. Same answer as Atlas!
That's what the Smudge wrote. It treated inches like tens and ones. A foot is 12 inches, not 10. 15 inches take away 12 inches is?
6 feet is 72 inches. 72 and how many more make 80?
2 feet is 24 inches. Add the 6 inches.
Hey, I'm Felix! I stomped on every board of this bridge to test it. The boards are strong. It's the rope rail that broke.
I change it all to inches first. 2 feet is 24 inches. Add 8 more inches: 32 inches in all. Then I work and change back.

Every 12 little inch marks make one foot. So 6 feet is 6 groups of 12 inches.
The north post stops 5 inches past 6 feet. The south post stops 7 inches past. They are 2 inches apart!
Picture the ruler: 12 inch marks make exactly 1 foot. This scrap is exactly 12 inches.
Picture the ruler. 2 feet is 2 groups of 12 inches, not 20. That's 24 inches, and 6 more.
Hi! I'm Hazel. I'm drawing the river today. Look how the water sparkles under the bridge!
I picture a ruler. Every 12 little inch marks make one big foot.

lines.t: In meters, we traded 100 centimeters. With feet, we trade 12 inches for 1 foot.
Watch the inches. When they reach 12, trade them for a new foot. Never at 10!
Careful! A foot is not 10 inches. A foot is 12 inches, so 10 inches is shorter than a foot.
That's the Smudge's trick! 12 is the inches in a foot. A yard is 3 feet, so 9 yards is 9 × 3 feet.
That's the Smudge's trick! 8 feet would be 96 inches, way too many. A foot is 12 inches, not 10. Count by 12s.
Hello, I'm Cora. Gus says nobody crosses until the rail is fixed. That's a good rule.
When the inches reach 12, trade them for 1 foot. Not 10. Twelve!

lines.t: Hi, {name}! I'm Rosa. I make all the rope in town.
Last night the Smudge snapped the rope rail on the bridge. Then it blew my rope scraps all over the riverbank!
Every scrap has a tag in inches. Please sort them into my three bins: SHORT, 1 FOOT and LONG.
A scrap that is exactly 1 foot goes in the 1 FOOT bin. Walk onto a sparkle to pick one up.
Every scrap is sorted. Thank you, {name}!
The 1-foot pieces go to Gus to help fix the rail. The rest I'll tie into new rope.
That rope you spliced is holding tight. Good knots and good math!
I measure every rope in feet and inches. 12 inches make 1 foot, every time.
